section_summary: This section contains Department of State correspondence and memoranda from September and October 1937 concerning American funds frozen in Japan as a result of Japanese foreign exchange controls. It includes an instruction to Ambassador Joseph C. Grew in Tokyo outlining U.S. policy against bilateral clearing agreements while directing the Embassy to monitor discrimination against American creditors and informally encourage exchange releases. Additionally, it features internal memoranda from the Adviser on International Economic Affairs analyzing the exchange control situation and transmitting a study of Japanese foreign exchange resources to Far Eastern Affairs officers.

subfiles.about: Instruction advising the American Ambassador in Tokyo on U.S. policy regarding American surplus funds blocked under Japanese exchange controls.
subfiles.summary: The Department rejects bilateral clearing agreements to liquidate frozen American funds in Japan, directing the Embassy to monitor discrimination and informally assist American creditors.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 134 to Ambassador Joseph C. Grew regarding American Funds Frozen in Japan

subfiles.about: Memorandum analyzing the Japanese exchange control situation and recommending against clearing agreements while seeking facts on discrimination against American funds.
subfiles.summary: Analyzing Japanese exchange controls, the Adviser opposes bilateral clearing agreements and recommends investigating whether blocked American funds suffer discriminatory treatment.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from the Adviser on International Economic Affairs on Japanese Exchange Controls and Frozen American Funds

subfiles.about: Transmittal memorandum confirming that a study of Japanese foreign exchange resources was checked with relevant government departments.
subfiles.summary: Transmittal note confirming that the enclosed study of Japanese foreign exchange resources was coordinated with other informed government departments.
subfiles.title: Memorandum regarding Study of Japanese Foreign Exchange Resources
subfiles.to: Stanley K. Hornbeck and Maxwell M. Hamilton
